sources.title: Ivermectin 20 years on: maturation of a wonder drug
sources.population: Review of ivermectin pharmacology and mechanisms in animals and humans
sources.preview: A 2005 review in Trends in Parasitology covering the mechanisms of ivermectin's selective activity, including its exclusion from the human central nervous system, and the role of P-glycoprotein at the blood-brain barrier.

sources.title: The effect of food on the pharmacokinetics of oral ivermectin
sources.design: Population pharmacokinetic analysis of pooled data from two single-dose trials
sources.population: Healthy volunteers (n=15 combined): 12 dosed after a high-fat breakfast, 3 dosed fasted; single oral dose of 12 mg ivermectin
sources.preview: Population pharmacokinetic analysis estimating the food effect of a high-fat breakfast on a single 12 mg oral dose of ivermectin: relative bioavailability 1.18 (95% CI 1.10-1.67), described by the authors as minimal.

sources.title: Ivermectin and permethrin for treating scabies
sources.design: Cochrane systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
sources.population: People with scabies of all ages and either sex; trials comparing permethrin or ivermectin
sources.preview: Cochrane review finding that oral ivermectin at a standard dose of 200 micrograms per kilogram may lead to slightly lower clearance rates than permethrin cream at one week but little or no difference by two to four weeks; one-dose and two-dose ivermectin regimens showed high-certainty evidence of little or no difference at four weeks.

sources.title: Oral ivermectin versus malathion lotion for difficult-to-treat head lice
sources.design: Multicenter, cluster-randomized, double-blind, double-dummy controlled trial
sources.population: 812 patients from 376 households with live head lice not eradicated by prior topical insecticide; minimum age 2 years, minimum weight 15 kg
sources.preview: Oral ivermectin at 400 micrograms per kilogram given on days 1 and 8 achieved 95.2% lice-free status at day 15, versus 85.0% with 0.5% malathion lotion (absolute difference 10.2 percentage points; 95% CI 4.6 to 15.7; p<0.001) in adults and children with difficult-to-treat head lice.

sources.title: Effect of ivermectin vs placebo on time to sustained recovery in outpatients with mild to moderate COVID-19: a randomized clinical trial
sources.population: 1,591 outpatients aged 30 and older with confirmed COVID-19 and two or more symptoms for seven days or less, enrolled at 93 US sites
sources.preview: ACTIV-6 platform trial: ivermectin 400 micrograms per kilogram daily for 3 days did not significantly improve time to sustained recovery versus placebo (HR 1.07; 95% CrI 0.96 to 1.17). Hospitalizations or deaths occurred in 1.2% of both groups.

guides.description: An antiparasitic with negative randomized COVID-19 findings and laboratory cancer research.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Oral ivermectin is used for strongyloidiasis and onchocerciasis. A higher-dose COVID-19 trial did not speed recovery; the cancer studies discussed here are preclinical.

questions.question: Why does ivermectin largely stay out of the human central nervous system, and when can that change?
questions.answer: The US prescribing information states that ivermectin does not readily cross the blood-brain barrier in humans, contributing to its selective toxicity against invertebrate parasites whose glutamate-gated chloride channels are the primary target. P-glycoprotein, an efflux transporter expressed at the blood-brain barrier, actively limits ivermectin's central nervous system exposure in mammals; a 2005 review of ivermectin's mechanisms in Trends in Parasitology discusses how this efflux system underlies the drug's selectivity profile. The label warns that neurotoxicity, including altered consciousness, confusion, stupor, coma and death, has been reported even at recommended doses; overdosage, and especially accidental exposure to veterinary formulations, substantially increases the risk.

sections.label: Benefits
sections.paragraph: Six days of higher-dose ivermectin did not improve sustained recovery from acute COVID-19. Ovarian, brain, breast and colorectal cancer experiments reported effects in cells or animals, without a patient benefit estimate from those experiments. The liver-cancer combination report is retracted and excluded from efficacy conclusions.

sections.label: Dosing
sections.title: What dosing schedules have been used?
sections.paragraph: The US label specifies a single oral dose of approximately 200 micrograms per kilogram for strongyloidiasis and approximately 150 micrograms per kilogram for onchocerciasis, both taken on an empty stomach with water. COVID-19 trials in the ACTIV-6 platform tested 400 micrograms per kilogram daily for 3 days and 600 micrograms per kilogram daily for 6 days; neither dose regimen improved sustained recovery.

questions.question: What is the labeled dose for treating strongyloidiasis?
questions.answer: The US prescribing information specifies a single oral dose of approximately 200 micrograms of ivermectin per kilogram of body weight for strongyloidiasis of the intestinal tract, taken on an empty stomach with water. The label provides a weight-band table: 15 to 24 kg, 1 tablet (3 mg); 25 to 35 kg, 2 tablets (6 mg); 36 to 50 kg, 3 tablets (9 mg); 51 to 65 kg, 4 tablets (12 mg); 66 to 79 kg, 5 tablets (15 mg); and 80 kg or above, 200 micrograms per kilogram. In general, additional doses are not necessary, though follow-up stool examinations should confirm eradication.

questions.question: What is the labeled dose for treating onchocerciasis, and how often is retreatment needed?
questions.answer: The US prescribing information specifies a single oral dose of approximately 150 micrograms of ivermectin per kilogram of body weight for onchocerciasis, taken on an empty stomach with water. The weight-band table runs from 15 to 25 kg (1 tablet, 3 mg) through 65 to 84 kg (4 tablets, 12 mg), with 150 micrograms per kilogram for individuals weighing 85 kg or above. Ivermectin kills the tissue microfilariae of Onchocerca volvulus but not the adult worms, so retreatment is required. For individual patients, retreatment may be considered at intervals as short as 3 months; mass distribution programs commonly use a 12-month interval.

questions.question: Does food affect how ivermectin is absorbed?
questions.answer: The US prescribing information directs patients to take ivermectin tablets on an empty stomach with water. A high-fat meal pharmacokinetic study at a supratherapeutic 30 mg dose found approximately 2.5-fold higher bioavailability compared with fasting, an effect that the label attributes to dose-dependent absorption dynamics. A 2020 population pharmacokinetic analysis published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy examined the food effect with a standard single oral dose of 12 mg ivermectin and estimated the relative bioavailability from a high-fat breakfast versus fasting at 1.18 (95% confidence interval 1.10 to 1.67), describing the effect as minimal at that dose.

questions.question: What dosing regimens did clinical trials use for scabies and head lice?
questions.answer: In a randomized controlled trial in the New England Journal of Medicine comparing oral ivermectin with malathion lotion for difficult-to-treat head lice, patients received 400 micrograms per kilogram on days 1 and 8, a seven-day interval; 95.2% were lice-free at day 15 with ivermectin versus 85.0% with malathion. A 2018 Cochrane systematic review of ivermectin and permethrin for scabies examined trials that used a standard oral ivermectin dose of 200 micrograms per kilogram; some trials included a second dose, and high-certainty evidence showed little or no difference in four-week clearance between one-dose and two-dose regimens. In the United States, oral ivermectin is used off-label for scabies, and neither a specific repeat interval nor a one-dose versus two-dose approach is established as a single standard regimen.

questions.question: What doses did COVID-19 trials test, and what did the results show?
questions.answer: The ACTIV-6 platform trial tested two ivermectin regimens in separate comparisons. The first, published in JAMA in 2022, enrolled 1,591 outpatients and tested 400 micrograms per kilogram daily for 3 days; the hazard ratio for time to sustained recovery was 1.07 (95% credible interval 0.96 to 1.17), not a significant improvement, and hospitalizations or deaths occurred in 1.2% of both the ivermectin and placebo groups. The second, published in JAMA in 2023, enrolled 1,206 participants and tested 600 micrograms per kilogram daily for 6 days; it also found no significant improvement in time to sustained recovery. Neither regimen reduced hospitalizations or deaths compared with placebo.
